counterexample: G = ({u,v}, {(u,v),(v,u)}) — a 2-cycle. GT = {(u,v),(v,u),(u,u),(v,v)}. Any H with |F| <= 1 cannot realize GT (a single edge gives at most one reachability pair beyond nothing), and the only 2-edge digraph on {u,v} whose closure is GT is {(u,v),(v,u)} itself: {(u,u),(v,v)} misses (u,v); {(u,v),(u,u)} misses (v,u); etc. So this G has a unique transitive reduction yet is not acyclic, refuting the 'unique => acyclic' direction the proof was supposed to establish.
reasoning_summary: Step-by-step check of lines 0001-0033. Setup (0009-0015) is fine: finite digraphs, paths of positive length, GT as the reachability digraph, transitive reduction = minimum-edge H with HT = GT. Theorem 1's DAG argument is sound so far: for an acyclic G reachability is a (strict) partial order (0018-0022, the 'partial order' wording is a harmless abuse since positive-length paths make the relation irreflexive on a DAG); the cover relation and Hasse diagram H are defined correctly (0023-0026); HT = GT for a finite poset is a correct standard fact (0027-0029); and the start of the minimality argument at 0030-0032 is valid — deleting a cover edge (u,v) leaves no u-v path, since any surviving path has length >= 2 and yields an intermediate w with u < w < v, contradicting coverage. The failure is at 0033: the text terminates mid-sentence (page marker '1'), so (a) the minimality argument is never completed — showing no edge of H is removable does not yet show H has the minimum edge count, which needs the further step that every H' with H'T = GT must contain all cover edges — (b) uniqueness in the DAG case is asserted but not proved, and (c) the 'only if' direction (unique transitive reduction => acyclic), which is the non-classical half of the biconditional, is never argued at all. Nothing that is present is mathematically false, but the proof as given does not establish the stated theorem. Moreover the unproved direction is itself false under the definitions the proof adopts: a 2-cycle is cyclic and has exactly one minimum-edge digraph realizing its closure, so no completion of this argument could succeed without extra hypotheses (e.g. restricting to strongly connected components of size >= 3).
